real_interpreter_evidence._purpose: Proof that the B3 bounded interpreter was actually run against a live model at least once, not only exercised through the deterministic_offline stub used everywhere else in this repository's tests and benchmarks.
real_interpreter_evidence._reproduce: export OPENAI_API_KEY=<your key>; export MANDATEGUARD_INTERPRETER_BASE_URL=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1; export MANDATEGUARD_INTERPRETER_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b; python3 -m bailiff.demo --real-interpreter
real_interpreter_evidence.fixture_case: R3_AMBIGUOUS bounded-interpreter case, generated by bailiff.demo.make_ambiguous_event
notes: The interpreter is an annotation service only: it returns one taxonomy reason and a confidence score. It cannot authorize a retry, change consent, or call the provider — that boundary is enforced in bailiff/guardrails.py, not by the model's good behaviour.

In this run the model's own confidence (0.9) still did not cross the threshold the guardrail engine requires to act on a model-sourced reason for this case shape, so the case still escalated to HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED with zero provider calls — the same outcome as the deterministic_offline stub. That is the point being demonstrated: the model is consulted, not trusted, and a wrong or low-confidence answer cannot widen what the runtime is willing to do.

model_cost_inr uses Groq's published list price for openai/gpt-oss-20b ($0.10/1M input, $0.50/1M output tokens as of August 2026), set via MANDATEGUARD_MODEL_INPUT_USD_PER_1M / MANDATEGUARD_MODEL_OUTPUT_USD_PER_1M, converted at the repository default of 85 INR/USD.
No API key is stored in this repository. Reproducing this run requires the operator's own key in OPENAI_API_KEY at run time.

method.crossover: lowest swept price at which a fully guarded arm (B2 or B3) becomes the recommended arm; null means no swept price makes a guarded arm win
method.harm_multiplier_curve: net value equals incremental recovered minus realized harm times the multiplier, minus human review cost and model cost; realized harm counts only prohibited actions that actually reached the provider
method.note: Both curves re-price one frozen benchmark run. No arm is re-executed, so every point on both curves reads the same ledger and the same decisions.
method.violation_cost_curve: net value equals incremental recovered minus independently detected violations times the flat cost, minus human review cost and model cost
